issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a parameterless ride method (messageOnRide(): String) — the UML and textual description state messageOnRide() should return "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]", and the template Main calls r.messageOnRide() with no arguments. However, the solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and implements messageOnRide(int speed) in Pig and Seal (including speed information in the returned string). This is a signature/parameter mismatch: students following the problem/template will implement a different method than exists in the provided solution, and the solution code would not compile against the template Main (which calls the no-arg method).
issues.suggested_fix:
Make the Rideable interface and its implementations consistent with the problem statement and template. Either:

1) Prefered fix (align solution to spec/template): Change Rideable.messageOnRide to a no-argument method returning String (String messageOnRide()), and update Pig and Seal to implement messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]" (no speed). This will match the UML, textual description, and the calls in Main.

Concretely, in the solution repository:
- solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Rideable.java: change to 'public interface Rideable { String messageOnRide(); }'
- solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Pig.java: implement 'public String messageOnRide() { return "Riding on Pig " + getName(); }'
- solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Seal.java: implement 'public String messageOnRide() { return "Riding on Seal " + getName(); }'

Or

2) If the intention was to include a speed parameter, update the problem statement UML, textual description, and the template Main to reflect messageOnRide(int speed) and adjust example calls (e.g., r.messageOnRide(5)). However, changing the problem/template is a larger specification change and is not recommended unless speed is intentionally part of the exercise.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and textual requirements) and the template expect a Rideable.messageOnRide() method with no parameters that returns a string like "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". The solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) (an int parameter) and implements Pig and Seal accordingly (returns include the speed and a different format). This is a direct identifier/signature mismatch for the same conceptual operation (the animal-ride message). Students following the problem and template will look for and call messageOnRide() with no arguments (the template's Main even calls r.messageOnRide()), but the solution's interface and implementations require an int argument, creating a compile/runtime mismatch and cognitive mapping confusion.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the Rideable API consistent with the problem statement and template. Either (A) change the solution to match the problem/template: define Rideable.messageOnRide() with no parameters and update Pig and Seal to implement messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]", or (B) if the intended design requires a speed, update the problem statement and template (including the example calls in Main and the UML) to declare messageOnRide(int speed) and show the expected return format. Prefer option A to minimize disruption and match the provided specification.
